title: Mini-onboard telemetry guardrails and probe cookbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact cookbook for the first 30–90 minutes of a new SDK integrator (internal or customer) focused on observability and safety: what telemetry we require, lightweight guardrails to ship initial telemetry, and a repeatable probe lab to validate latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- New teams often ship SDK usage without consistent telemetry (we see missing model_version, route, env, and correlation ids).
- That gap leads to hard-to-debug performance regressions and false positives in quality alerts.
- We want a tiny onboarding artifact that pairs the quickstart SDK experience with minimum viable telemetry and 6 probe checks (probe lab) that catch the most common early issues.

Audience:
- SDK integrators: quick internal adopters, partners, early customers.
- Eng-oncall/observability: needs to know what signals to expect.
- Solutions engineers onboarding customers.

Non-goals:
- Full production telemetry spec (Confluence link above is canonical).
- Exhaustive alerting rules.

High-level goals (success criteria):
- New SDK sample app emits the telemetry contract within first 30 minutes.
- Probe lab detects latency regressions >2x baseline, per-token cost anomalies, and model mismatch (wrong model_version) in a repeatable way.
- Integrator can run smoke checks locally and get a pass/fail report.

Minimum telemetry contract (MVT) — fields we require on every request/response pair:
- request_id (UUID)
- sdk_client (string, e.g. js/py/java + version)
- model (string)
- model_version (string)
- route (string) -- logical route or endpoint name
- env (string: dev/staging/prod)
- token_count_request (int)
- token_count_response (int)
- latency_ms (int) -- end-to-end client-observed latency
- status_code (int) -- 200, 4xx, 5xx mapping from SDK
- kv_tags (optional map but proto: comma-delimited key=value pairs)

Implementation patterns (quick):
- Node/Python SDKs: automatic header injection at client level. Enforce via lint rule in example app.
- For serverless or browser: fallback to localUUID + sticky device id if no central correlation.

Quickstart: 10 minute path
1) Clone minimal sample app (internal quick git link)
   git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples-sdk-mini.git 
2) Install and configure (node example):
   cp .env.example .env
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<<sandbox_key>>
   npm install
3) Start local harness (runs example and telemetry shim):
   npm run dev -- --telemetry=console
4) Run smoke command (single script does 6 probes):
   ./scripts/run-probes.sh --api-key $REDWOOD_API_KEY
5) Check output: should see "MVT OK" and 6 probe lines with PASS/FAIL.

Probe lab (6 minimal experiments) — run order and what to check:
- Probe 1: Model handshake
  - Call metadata endpoint: get model_version and hash; fail if mismatch with config.
  - Detect: model not available or model_version missing.
- Probe 2: Cold-start latency sample
  - 3 warmup requests, 5 measured single-shot requests at 1s gap.
  - Fail if median latency > target (configurable per model).
- Probe 3: Prefix KL/quality smoke
  - Send 5 prompt variations; check output tokens for early truncation, repeated tokens, or empty responses.
- Probe 4: Token accounting sanity
  - Verify token_count_request + token_count_response roughly match local tokenizer estimate (±15%).
- Probe 5: Cost anomaly detector
  - Run 10 batched requests with two batch sizes; compute per-token cost delta vs baseline; alert if >30% variance.
- Probe 6: Error surface and retry behavior
  - Simulate 429/503 via local fault-injector; validate SDK retries respect backoff policy and expose telemetry for each attempt.

Pass/fail gating (first-pass rules):
- FAIL: missing model_version or request_id in telemetry -> block promotion.
- FAIL: error rate >2% on 100 synthetic requests -> block.
- WARN: per-token cost variance >20% -> flag for review.

Local smoke harness outputs (example):
- Summary: MVT OK, probes PASSED: 5/6 (Probe 5 WARNING: cost variance).
- Logs (excerpt):
  2025-02-07T14:03:12Z request_id=1a2b3c sdk_client=js-0.12.4 model=redwood-ggml model_version=v2 route=chat env=dev latency_ms=243 token_in=9 token_out=47 status=200

Telemetry pitfalls (notes to self / common gotchas):
- Users strip headers in proxies; add SDK-level fallback to include metadata as JSON in first response body if header injection blocked.
- Browser embedding: CORS + exposure of API key -> use proxy; ensure proxy copies telemetry fields.
- Mobile: batching at client can hide per-request telemetry; include batch->subrequest mapping ids.

Lightweight alert templates (to export to PagerDuty or Alertmanager):
- Alert: "SDK telemetry missing model_version" threshold=5 missing in 10m -> page oncall.
- Alert: "Per-token cost spike" if 10m rolling median per-token cost > 2x baseline -> notify billing & SE.
- Alert: "Client observed latency p95 > SLO" -> page prod-sre.

Developer checklist for an integrator (copy into onboarding checklist):
- [ ] Run quickstart sample app and confirm MVT OK
- [ ] Execute probe lab, confirm all PASS or document WARNs
- [ ] Add SDK client string to env and bump semver in example
- [ ] Commit telemetry fixture (small JSON) into repo for CI smoke tests
- [ ] Open PR against examples repo and link GH PR to onboarding tracker (GHI-3421)

CI ideas (fast wins):
- Add a GitHub Action that runs the probe lab against a staging route nightly; fail on any FAIL probe.
- Upload summary telemetry artifact as job output for triage.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Do we force model_version at API surface (server-side) or rely on client to send it? (tradeoff: server can stamp, but we lose client-side intent signal.)
- How to best represent kv_tags in a compact string without breaking header size limits? Need agreement with infra about header quota.
- Add a tiny E2E example for Dedicated customers that shows local telemetry routing to on-prem Kinesis.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Priya: create the GitHub Action skeleton and CI probe runner (ETA 2025-02-14).
- Jonah: verify header size policy with infra and report back (ETA 2025-02-10).
- Aisha: wire this doc into onboarding template and add to SDK quickstart README (ETA 2025-02-07).

Appendix: quick SDK snippets
- Node: automatic header injection (pseudocode)
  const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, telemetry: {sdk_client: `js-${pkg.version}`, env: process.env.ENV}})
  await client.generate({model: 'redwood-alpha', prompt: 'hello'});

- Python: minimal check that telemetry fields are emitted
  resp = client.generate(...)
  assert 'request_id' in resp.metadata
  assert resp.metadata['model_version'] != ''

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally compact and pragmatic. The goal is not perfection but repeatability: a developer should be able to run this doc's quickstart and get reproducible PASS/FAIL guidance for the first integration milestone.
- If you make changes, keep the MVT minimal and backwards compatible (adding opt-in fields is fine, removing required fields needs a migration plan).

History:
- v0.1 (2025-01-08) initial draft (Aisha)
- v0.2 (2025-02-07) added probe lab and CI ideas (collab edits)

---
End of doc.
